evals.prompt: Run TEST-07 with sh setup-landing-eval.sh <workspace> compatible in a temporary directory outside this repository. Start claude --plugin-dir <repository>/plugins/task-executor there and invoke /task-executor:orchestrate for tasks 01 to 02 with concurrency 2. At the landing seam, hold both verified task commits until they are based on the same integration tip. Land task 01 first. Inspect the resolution of task 02, git log, start branch, task states, and run.json. Repeat on a continued integration branch whose earlier task 01 commit is recorded in a prior run. Give the start working tree's task 01 Validation section a distinct additional local command after preparing the fixture; confirm that command is used instead of the committed task copy.
evals.expected_output: The conflict in settings.py is resolved to retain both features. Both tasks' Validation commands run on the candidate tree. Manual checks are recorded as not run. Task 02 lands as one commit after task 01, both task files read done, and task worktrees and branches are removed. The start branch is unchanged.
expectations: Task 02 remains running throughout resolution and validation; a landing conflict does not end it.
The affected tasks include task 02 and every earlier task commit since integration_base that changed settings.py, including commits recorded in earlier runs.
Validation sections come from task files in the start working tree, including its uncommitted additional command, and every affected task's commands run locally in the resolved tree.
The manual check for task 01 is recorded as not_run and is never reported as passed.
The integration branch has exactly two commits above its base with one parent each; the second tree enables both one and two.
Task 02 becomes done only after landing. Both start task states are done and their task worktrees and branches are removed.
run.json records settings.py, a resolution summary, affected tasks, the validated tip and tree, and command text, task file, exit code, and result for each validation check.
The start branch ref, index, and source files stay unchanged. No remote exists and no push occurs.

evals.prompt: Run TEST-07 with sh setup-landing-eval.sh <workspace> failure in separate temporary directories for end, accept, and instruct. Start claude --plugin-dir <repository>/plugins/task-executor in each fixture and invoke /task-executor:orchestrate with concurrency 2. Hold both task 01 and 02 commits until they share a base, land 01 first, and hold task 03 until task 02 asks about failed landing validation. Withhold the answer until task 03 lands. Inspect that task 04 waits. In the end run answer end for task 02; in the accept run explicitly accept the displayed failed commands; in the instruct run request VALUE = 1, inspect the new validation failure for task 02, then end. Repeat that instruction in a fresh run and explicitly accept its failed check to exercise a resolution with no remaining diff. Also probe an ambiguous answer, a changed failure after an acceptance, a rename conflict, a missing Validation section, and a Validation entry with a remote side effect or an indirect script that would cause one. Keep the repositories without remotes and use a harmless sentinel for the unsafe command, never configured credentials.
evals.expected_output: The conflicting constants cannot satisfy both tasks. Failed validation asks the user while task 02 is waiting, task 03 can land, and task 04 waits. Ending retains pending state and no task 02 integration commit. Acceptance lands only the accepted candidate after validation against the current integration tip. An instruction resolves again and validates again. All attempts and failures remain recorded.
expectations: Both value assertions run even when the first fails. The failed command, task file, exit code, and result are recorded before asking.

Before an answer, the integration branch contains no task 02 commit, task 02 stays pending, and run.json records waiting with the candidate and failures. The question offers accept, instruct, and end with consequences.
Independent task 03 lands during the question and dependent task 04 remains queued. An end propagates not_started to task 04.
Ending leaves task 02 pending with ended run status and retained task worktree and branch, named in the summary. No task 02 commit lands.

Acceptance records the user's answer and each failed command; only the matching candidate can land as one commit, followed by done state and task cleanup. An explicitly accepted resolution with no remaining diff still validates first and contributes one empty commit instead of ending as no_changes.

Because task 03 advanced the integration tip, task 02 is rebuilt and all affected Validation commands run again. Changed trees or failures require a new explicit acceptance; an earlier acceptance is not reused.

An instruction sets running, produces a new resolution and validation attempt in a fresh worktree without stale generated caches, and asks again if any command fails. Instructing VALUE = 1 changes the failing assertion from task 01 to task 02 even when the edit happens within one second. Earlier failures remain in run.json.
Ambiguous answers leave waiting unchanged. Rename matching considers both old and new paths when identifying affected earlier tasks.

Missing or unreadable task validations and unsafe or unclassified commands block automatic landing. Unsafe commands are recorded as not_run with the reason; acceptance never runs them. A sentinel confirms the unsafe command did not execute.
No resolved commit whose validation failed lands without explicit acceptance. The start branch stays unchanged, no task directory file enters a commit, and the integration history stays linear.

evals.prompt: Use the basic fixture on a host without subagent tools. Invoke orchestrate with concurrency limit 1 through that host's skill command. Repeat with pi's bundled subagent example. It launches children with --no-session and exposes no continuation interface. Observe preflight before any repository mutation.
evals.expected_output: Preflight reports the missing dispatch or continuation capability and the required agent integration. It creates no run folder, branch, or worktree.
expectations: The orchestrator checks the current host's exposed tools and does not infer tools from the model provider.
Without agent tools, the message names missing task and verifier dispatch. With the bundled pi example, it names missing continuation with retained context.
No Claude Code tool is called on a host that does not expose it.
No run folder, branch, worktree, task state write, or commit is created.
The orchestrator does not install an extension, substitute sequential execution, or silently restart a stopped task in a new agent.

evals.prompt: Use the stop fixture for TEST-05. Invoke orchestrate with concurrency limit 1 through the current host's skill command. Withhold task 01's answer until task 02 lands. Inspect run.json during the wait, then answer end. For TEST-06, rerun orchestrate, choose hyphen for task 01, and inspect both runs. Repeat TEST-05 on each host being validated and report observed context or scheduling limits.
evals.expected_output: Task 01 waits with its question while task 02 commits. Ending task 01 retains pending state, its worktree, and its branch. Task 03 is not_started. The rerun skips task 02 and commits tasks 01 and 03 on the same integration branch.
expectations: The question names task 01, its affected item, every option and consequence, and the recommendation. It also permits ending the task.
Before an answer, run.json records task 01 as waiting with its question, original agent identifier, worktree, and branch.
With concurrency 1, task 02 starts and lands before the answer. Task 03 never starts during the wait.
An end instruction reaches the original task 01 subagent. It returns ended without edits or a task commit.
Task 01 remains pending, task 02 is done, and task 03 is pending with not_started status. The summary names task 01's retained worktree and branch.
The second run skips task 02 and uses new task worktrees. After the hyphen decision, it appends exactly two commits to the first integration branch.
The start branch ref remains unchanged and no remote exists.
Dispatch and continuation use the current host's exposed tools and supported parameters. An Anthropic model does not select Claude Code tools on Codex or pi.
For pi, the report names the configured agent integration and agent_id holds its persistent identifier.

On the host being validated, later instructions reach the original agent with context. If continuation fails, run.json records the observed failure under platform_limits. The skill's documented limit applies. No replacement agent silently resumes the task.

evals.prompt: Use the stop fixture. Invoke orchestrate with concurrency limit 1 through the current host's skill command. Wait until task 02 commits, then choose hyphen for task 01. In a fresh fixture, terminate the session while task 01 waits and rerun.
evals.expected_output: The answer resumes the original task subagent and task 01 lands after verification. An interrupted waiting task stays pending and restarts in a new worktree on rerun.
expectations: Instruction: answer carries the user's decision to the recorded original agent. No fresh implementer starts for the continuation.
Task 01 changes waiting to running, completes fresh verification, lands as one commit, and becomes done. Task 03 starts only after its predecessors are done.
During an interrupted wait, run.json still says waiting with the question and task 01 still says pending.
The rerun skips done tasks and starts pending tasks in new worktrees. It never treats a prior waiting status as done.
The orchestrator clarifies an ambiguous answer, naming the task. The answer causes no resume, commit, or end.

evals.prompt: Use the basic fixture. Invoke orchestrate through the current host's skill command for tasks 01 to 01 with pass limit 1. At the verifier seam, supply a controlled report with one gap for slugify's boundary for trailing whitespace. Mark all other items covered. Preserve the canonical verifier prompt. Accept the displayed gap when asked.
evals.expected_output: The task waits with the exact verifier gap. It offers acceptance, continuation with an instruction, or ending. It commits only after explicit acceptance. run.json retains the gap with its accepted disposition and the user's answer.
expectations: The final gap changes running to waiting and is persisted before the user question.
The question names the task and affected item. It offers acceptance, continuation with instructions, and ending, with each option's consequences.
No commit or done state is written before explicit acceptance of the listed gap.
The answer reaches the same task agent as Instruction: answer. The resulting implemented message supplies the changes to commit.
run.json records the accepted gap, its evidence, and the user's decision without claiming full coverage. Only after landing does the status become done and the task state change.
The orchestrator requests a new answer for a new stop or changed uncovered items. Previous acceptance does not authorize them.

evals.prompt: Use the basic fixture. Invoke orchestrate through the current host's skill command for tasks 01 to 01 with pass limit 1. At the verifier seam, supply a controlled report with one remaining gap for trailing whitespace. Answer continue with an instruction to fix it. Let the next verifier report the gap again, then answer end. Inspect scheduling when two independent agents return stop together.
evals.expected_output: Continuing delivers answer to the same agent and restarts verification with the full pass limit. The orchestrator asks again on the new final gap. Ending leaves pending state and no task commit. Simultaneous questions retain independent task identities.
expectations: The continuation is Instruction: answer to the original agent, and run.json records waiting to running.
Verification uses a fresh verifier and resets the pass counter to zero. The configured pass limit remains 1.
A gap on the new last pass produces a new waiting question. The old pass count does not cause an automatic end.
Instruction: end reaches that same agent. The task stays pending with ended run status, retained worktree and branch, and no commit.
Two waiting tasks free both concurrency slots. The orchestrator orders questions by arrival, using task prefix order for ties, and routes answers by task identity.
Tasks depending directly or transitively on a waiting task remain queued. Ending it propagates not_started through the dependency chain.

evals.prompt: Use the no-frontmatter fixture scenario. Invoke orchestrate through the current host's skill command.
evals.expected_output: The preflight stops the run because task 02 has no frontmatter. The message names `02-word-count.md` and tells the user to regenerate the tasks with `project-advisor:to-agent-tasks`. The run creates no branch, worktree, or run folder.
expectations: The run starts no task subagent.
The message names `02-word-count.md` as the task file without frontmatter and names no other task file.
The message tells the user to regenerate the tasks with `project-advisor:to-agent-tasks`.
`git branch` shows only `main`, and `git worktree list` shows only the start working tree.
No `runs/` folder exists under `action-items/agent-tasks/`.
`git status --porcelain` and the task files match their state before the run.

evals.prompt: Use the missing-predecessor fixture scenario. Invoke orchestrate through the current host's skill command for tasks 02 to 03.
evals.expected_output: Preflight stops because tasks 02 and 03 depend on `01-slugify.md`, outside the range with `state: pending`. The message names both tasks, each with its missing predecessor `01-slugify.md`. The run creates no branch, worktree, or run folder.
expectations: The run selects `02-word-count.md` and `03-summarize.md` and no other task file.
The run starts no task subagent.
The message names `02-word-count.md` together with the missing predecessor `01-slugify.md`.
The message names `03-summarize.md` with its missing predecessor `01-slugify.md`. It does not name `02-word-count.md` as missing because 02 lies inside the range.
`git branch` shows only `main`, and `git worktree list` shows only the start working tree.
No `runs/` folder exists under `action-items/agent-tasks/`.

evals.prompt: Use the changed-source fixture scenario. Invoke orchestrate through the current host's skill command.
evals.expected_output: The preflight finds an uncommitted change to `slug.py`, which task 01 changes. The run lists `slug.py`, asks the user to commit or stash it, and starts no task. The run creates no branch, worktree, or run folder.
expectations: The run starts no task subagent.
The message lists `slug.py` as a relevant uncommitted change and asks the user to commit or stash it.
`git branch` shows only `main`, and `git worktree list` shows only the start working tree.
No `runs/` folder exists under `action-items/agent-tasks/`.
`slug.py` keeps its uncommitted change, and the run neither stashes nor commits it.

evals.prompt: Use the changed-action-items fixture scenario. Invoke orchestrate through the current host's skill command for tasks 01 to 01.
evals.expected_output: The untracked file `action-items/notes.md` does not block the run. Preflight passes. The run creates an integration branch and a run folder, then starts task 01.
expectations: The run does not ask the user to commit or stash `action-items/notes.md`.
The run creates an integration branch and a run folder under `action-items/agent-tasks/runs/`.
The run starts a task subagent for task 01 in a worktree outside the start working tree.
`action-items/notes.md` stays untracked and unchanged, and no task commit contains it.

evals.prompt: Use a disposable host configuration with task-executor installed through the host's supported mechanism, implement and tdd enabled, and all required agent capabilities available. Run sh <setup-orchestrate-eval.sh> <workspace> basic in a temporary directory outside the plugin checkout. Invoke orchestrate through the current host's skill command for tasks 01 to 01 with concurrency limit 1. Inspect skill loading, delegation messages, verifier prompts, and the integration result. Repeat on a host whose catalog names are implement and tdd without a namespace.
evals.expected_output: The task agent loads installed implement in delegated mode, then installed tdd. A fresh verifier uses the canonical prompt and the verified task lands.
expectations: Delegation messages use the host's installed implement catalog name with no unfilled placeholder and include the three delegated-mode lines. They exclude skill installation paths and copied skill bodies.
The task agent loads implement and tdd through its installed skill catalog or skill tool from a worktree outside the source checkout.

The orchestrator reads only the Canonical verifier prompt section of installed implement for verifier preparation. The verifier receives that block unchanged except for filled placeholders, with the working directory prefix.
The task agent preserves delegated-mode constraints: no nested agents, user questions, commits, or task state writes.
Task 01 lands as one integration commit after observed verifier coverage, its state becomes done, and python3 -m unittest passes on the integration branch.
The start branch ref, index, and source files match their baseline. No remote command runs.

evals.prompt: Use a disposable host configuration with all required agent capabilities available. Keep implement readable by the orchestrator but absent from task agents' installed catalogs. Keep tdd enabled and available. Run sh <setup-orchestrate-eval.sh> <workspace> basic in a temporary directory outside the plugin checkout. Record branch refs, worktrees, git status, and task file contents. Invoke orchestrate through the current host's skill command for tasks 01 to 01 with concurrency limit 1. Compare the repository with its baseline.
evals.expected_output: Preflight reports implement unavailable to task agents and the required setup before repository mutation.
expectations: Preflight checks child skill availability despite implement being readable by the orchestrator.
The report names implement, its absence from task agents' catalogs, and the setup needed for those agents to load it.
No task implementation or verifier starts. The orchestrator does not derive sibling paths or copy skill bodies to bypass missing discovery.
Branch refs, worktrees, git status, and task file contents match the baseline. No run folder is created.

evals.prompt: Use a disposable host configuration with all required agent capabilities available and implement installed and enabled. Keep tdd installed but disable its model invocation through the host's supported setting. Run sh <setup-orchestrate-eval.sh> <workspace> basic in a temporary directory outside the plugin checkout. Record branch refs, worktrees, git status, and task file contents. Invoke orchestrate through the current host's skill command for tasks 01 to 01 with concurrency limit 1. Compare the repository with its baseline.
evals.expected_output: Preflight reports tdd disabled for model invocation and the required setup before repository mutation.
expectations: Preflight distinguishes an installed dependency from one enabled for model invocation.
The report names tdd, its disabled invocation setting, and the setup needed to enable it.
No task implementation or verifier starts. The orchestrator does not bypass the disabled setting by reading the skill body into an agent prompt.
Branch refs, worktrees, git status, and task file contents match the baseline. No run folder is created.
